section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion interprets findings that sexual minority women reported slightly higher body appreciation and a higher mean body size, though effect sizes were very small; the correlation between BMI and body appreciation was reported as stronger for heterosexual women but Fisher's r-to-z (z = .41, p = .34) indicated no significant difference. The section notes limitations including a primarily educated White sample, two cross-sectional samples collected at different time points, missing race/ethnicity data due to a technical error, and calls for more diverse, longitudinal, and nuanced research on sexual orientation subgroups.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'sexual minority women reported a higher mean body size and more appreciation for their bodies...'; 'the correlation between BMI and BAS is stronger for heterosexual women...'; 'using Fisher's r-to-z transformation, we found... (z=.41, p=.34)'; 'The study is comprised of primarily educated White women...'; 'the two samples were collected at two different points in time.'
